recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future source changes should be handled through resource-specific workflow alignment trackers and current work-group decisions rather than reopening FHIR-38870 as a blanket edit.
issue_request: FHIR-38870 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked that request resources align with Request pattern fields, especially basedOn, groupIdentifier, intent, requester, subject, and category. The final resolution required tooling to flag missing mappings, warn on unmapped or divergent pattern elements, render exception explanations in pattern summary tables, and raise or drive WG follow-up trackers.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly names FHIR-38870. The application appears in R5-era mapping infrastructure: 086649a235 added request mapping exception files for 15 request-pattern resources, bd2e3c688f added Contract request mapping exceptions, and e007e5da7d updated logical mapping templates. The Jira closure comment states that robust alignment ran out of time for R5 but the tooling was complete and producing warnings/info messages for R6 follow-up.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps the request-pattern extension spreadsheet active, tools/templates/template-logical.html renders logical mapping summaries, and current source has request mapping exception files documenting divergent and unmapped pattern elements. A current scan of Jira-listed artifacts found active resources have Request mappings and/or request mapping exception files, while historical SupplyRequest and Transport entries are outside current fhir.ini build scope; FHIR-53052 later removed Transport's stale Request mapping. Later applied trackers such as FHIR-43446, FHIR-43447, FHIR-43453, and FHIR-51718 show the intended resource-specific follow-up process.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Adding all Request fields or mappings wholesale from this seed would overrun the approved disposition and duplicate later WG-specific decisions.
